newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Aug 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Front page story says the fundamental task for the Communist Party is to develop social productive forces.
- Premier Li Peng says China should try to build a comprehensive nationwide transport network.
- Beijing city government to launch major campaign between mid-August and early October to crack down on pornographic and illegal publications.
- Official magazine calls for political negotiations to improve relations between China and Taiwan.
- China has 39 million pager users.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Front page story says reforms in China's state-owned enterprises have seen steady progress in the past five years.
-- China's largest city, Shanghai, has invested 3.5 billion yuan in and provided over 200 million yuan of assistance for central and western China.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Minister of Power Industry Shi Dazhen says power industry should use domestic and international financial markets to raise funds.
- Insurance business income in Beijing rises 61 percent to 3.95 billion yuan in first half.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China's machinery industry output value hits 62.22 billion yuan in first half, up 6.7 percent year-on-year, ending 26 months of losses
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- Direct losses from natural disasters hit 230 billion yuan in 1996.
MARKET DAILY
- First phase of Zhungeer Coal Field in Xinjiang region to go into operation in October.
- Construction Bank of China profits from foreign exchange reach $125.66 million in first half, up 38 percent year-on-year
CHINA DAILY
- Ministry of Civil Affairs and Foreign Ministry promulgate regulations on marriage registrations of Chinese living overseas.
- Ministry of Civil Affairs issues regulations on burial and funeral administration.
- Ministry of Public Security calls for safety measures to curb fires in petrochemical firms and other inflammable and explosion-prone areas.
